gaps.sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
gaps.explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'What time does the bank open?' she asked. She asked what time the bank ___.
gaps.explanation: The question reverts to statement word order and the verb backshifts: opens → opened.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: "Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
